data.gender_notes: Vinicia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'Vinicus', meaning 'conquering' or 'victorious'. In Christian tradition, it is the name of a martyred saint, celebrated on January 22. The name Vinicia carries the meaning “Victorious, Conquering” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Vinicia usually hope their child will grow to embody victorious, conquering and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength and victory over adversity.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vinicia total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: ויניציה
in_hebrew.meaning: השם ויניציה נגזר מלטינית ומשמעותו יין או כרם
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ויניציה הוא נגזר מהמילה הלטינית 'וינום' שפירושה יין. הוא קשור גם למילה 'ויטיס' שפירושה גפן או כרם. השם עשוי להיות קשור למסורות נוצריות הקושרות יין וגפן לסמלים של ישו והאוקריסטיה. השם ויניציה עשוי לשאת משמעות רוחנית של שמחה, שפע וברכה.

in_greek.name: Βινικία
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Βινικία προέρχεται από το λατινικό όνομα και σημαίνει κρασί ή αμπέλι
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βινικία είναι παράγωγο της λατινικής λέξης 'vinum' που σημαίνει κρασί. Στην ελληνική παράδοση, το αμπέλι και το κρασί έχουν συμβολική σημασία, αντιπροσωπεύοντας την αφθονία και τη χαρά. Το όνομα μπορεί να έχει συνδεθεί με τις πρώτες χριστιανικές παραδόσεις που συσχετίζουν το κρασί με τη Θεία Κοινωνία.

in_latin.name: Vinicia

historical_references.reference: Vinicia was the name of a Roman colony founded in 295 BC in the region of Umbria. The city was later renamed as Julia Vinicia in honor of Julius Caesar in 44 BC.
historical_references.context: The name Vinicia is believed to have originated from the Latin word 'vincere' meaning 'to conquer'. The city was strategically located and became an important center for trade and commerce.

historical_references.reference: During the Middle Ages, Vinicia was the name of a town located in what is now modern-day Romania. It was known as an important pilgrimage site due to the presence of a shrine dedicated to Saint Vincent of Saragossa.
historical_references.context: The name Vinicia is believed to be derived from the Latin word 'Vincentius', meaning 'conqueror of animals'. The town became a significant stop on the pilgrimage route to the Holy Land, attracting thousands of pilgrims each year.
